newsitem.title: USA: Digital Q4 seen in line, improved margins.
newsitem.headline: Digital Q4 seen in line, improved margins.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp's fourth quarter earnings were in line with most Wall Street estimates, with better-than-expected profit margins, but revenues were on the light side, some analysts said.

"It was OK, not great," said Steve Milunovich, a Morgan Stanley analyst. "Revenues are a little light, margins were a little better." Milunovich said that its new stock buyback plan will likely be viewed positively by investors.
Digital reported a profit of $0.75 a share, which was two cents better than the Wall Street consensus estimate of $0.73 a share. It also said it would buy back 15 million shares.
"It's a good number," said one technology stock trader. "It's exactly in line...Gross margins were slightly better than expected. The best part is they didn't blow up."
Digital said its gross profit margins of 34.6 percent of revenues were its best gross margins in more than three years.
Milunovich said that Digital also had a slightly lower tax rate, which also helped profits in the quarter.
Digital shares jumped 2-1/8, to 41-7/8, at the opening of the U.S. stock market, in part because the company's share buyback and its positive comments.
In its press release, Digital said it is its best position since the mid 1980s.
